elements.label: Figure 3.5
elements.description: Stacked bar chart of population (millions) by economic class, for ethnic minority and Kinh households in six regions, 2020. Y-axis: Population (millions), 0 to 25 in steps of 5. Legend (left to right): Extreme poor, Moderate poor, Economically vulnerable, Economically secure, Middle class. Categories (x-axis, paired Ethnic minority and Kinh bars): Midlands & Northern Mountains (ethnic minority ~7.0 total, with ~4.6 economically vulnerable and ~6.8 secure, middle class ~0.1; Kinh ~5.7 total, ~4.6 secure, ~1.0 middle class); Red River Delta (ethnic minority ~0.5 total, mostly secure; Kinh ~23.5 total, ~16.4 cumulative to secure, ~7 middle class); Northern & Coastal Central Region (ethnic minority ~2.4 total; Kinh ~17.8 total, ~14.6 cumulative to secure, ~3.2 middle class); Central Highlands (ethnic minority ~2.0 total; Kinh ~3.8 total, ~3.1 cumulative to secure, ~0.7 middle class); Southeast (ethnic minority ~1.0 total, mostly secure; Kinh ~16.4 total, ~8.5 cumulative to secure, ~7.9 middle class); Mekong Delta (ethnic minority ~1.2 total, all secure; Kinh ~15.8 total, ~14.0 cumulative to secure, ~1.8 middle class). Values are approximate readings (~). Pattern: Kinh households dominate the population in the Red River Delta, Northern & Coastal Central Region, Southeast and Mekong Delta, with the largest middle-class shares in the Red River Delta and Southeast; ethnic minority bars are much smaller and mostly composed of moderate poor, vulnerable and secure households. Note: Based on ethnicity of the household head. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2020.

elements.label: Figure 3.6
elements.description: Line chart of poverty rates among ethnic minority households, 2010-2020. Y-axis: Poverty rate (%), 0 to 80 in steps of 10. X-axis: 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020. Legend: Central Highlands (teal), Midlands & Northern Mountains (grey), Mekong Delta (orange), Northern & Coastal Central Region (yellow), Red River Delta (blue), Southeast (green). Approximate readings (~): Central Highlands ~73, ~62, ~65, ~47, ~52, ~47; Midlands & Northern Mountains ~60, ~52, ~52, ~38, ~38, ~28; Mekong Delta ~38, ~23, ~14, ~10, ~5, ~11; Northern & Coastal Central Region ~64, ~60, ~56, ~47, ~36, ~28; Red River Delta ~57, ~32, ~32, ~7, ~24, ~9; Southeast ~10, ~3, ~7, ~2, ~3, ~4. Pattern: poverty rates fall over the decade for most groups, with Central Highlands and Midlands & Northern Mountains highest, and Southeast lowest throughout; Red River Delta is volatile. Note: Poverty rate according to the $3.20/day 2011PPP poverty line. Poverty rates among the EM sample in Red River Delta is more variable due to small sample size. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2010-2020.

elements.label: Figure 3.7
elements.description: Line chart of poverty rates among Kinh households, 2010-2020. Y-axis: Poverty rate (%), 0 to 15 in steps of 3. X-axis: 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020. Legend: Central Highlands (teal), Midlands & Northern Mountains (grey), Mekong Delta (orange), Northern & Coastal Central Region (yellow), Red River Delta (blue), Southeast (green). Approximate readings (~): Central Highlands ~9, ~5.7, ~7.3, ~3.7, ~2.2, ~1.6; Midlands & Northern Mountains ~12, ~8.5, ~7.2, ~3.5, ~1.0, ~1.0; Mekong Delta ~12, ~10.2, ~6.2, ~4.0, ~1.8, ~3.1; Northern & Coastal Central Region ~11.8, ~7.3, ~6.0, ~2.2, ~1.6, ~1.1; Red River Delta ~7.8, ~4.3, ~3.2, ~1.3, ~0.9, ~0.3; Southeast ~5.0, ~3.0, ~1.9, ~0.2, ~0.2, ~0.3. Pattern: Kinh poverty rates decline steeply from 2010 to 2016 and then flatten at low levels by 2018-2020, with the Red River Delta and Southeast lowest. Note: Poverty rate according to the $3.20/day 2011PPP poverty line. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2010-2020.
